articleTitle: A Global-Local Attention Mechanism for Relation Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Relation classification, a crucial component of relation extraction, involves identifying connections between two entities. Previous studies have predominantly focused on integrating the attention mechanism into relation classification at a global scale, overlooking the importance of the local context. To address this gap, this paper introduces a novel global-local attention mechanism for relation classification, which enhances global attention with a localized focus. Additionally, we propose innovative hard and soft localization mechanisms to identify potential keywords for local attention. By incorporating both hard and soft localization strategies, our approach offers a more nuanced and comprehensive understanding of the contextual cues that contribute to effective relation classification. Our experimental results on the SemEval-2010 Task 8 dataset highlight the superior performance of our method compared to previous attention-based approaches in relation classification.

articleTitle: Improved Yolov4-tiny for Fire Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Fire disasters is one of the most frequent and widespread major disasters that threaten public safety and social development, causing property damage, casualties, ecological damage, social impact, and even climate change. Therefore, how to effectively reduce the losses caused by fire accidents has become an important research topic. Traditional methods based on sensors and computer imaging are used to detect fire accidents, but they have the drawback of having a small sensing area and a high false alarm rate. Image object detection technology is an important research topic in the field of machine learning, and has been widely applied in intelligent video analysis, achieving good application results, especially Yolov4-tiny, which has been widely applied in lightweight object detection. For flame target detection, Yolov4-tiny still has the problems of low accuracy and weights size, which is not conducive to deployment on low computing power devices. This paper improves the Yolov4-tiny model, achieving a high accuracy even with low weights size. The main improvements include modifying the backbone network and adding an output layer. We constructed a flame dataset and conducted experimental verification, and the results showed that the proposed method effectively reduced the weight size and improved accuracy; This is an effective method for deploying flame detection models on low computing power devices.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Cross-Shaped Microstrip Antenna Based on Ti3C2Tx MXene
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper proposed a single-fed, dual-frequency nested rectangular slot cross-shaped microstrip patch antenna which was printed on a FR4 substrate using Ti3C2Tx MXene film as the radiating element. The antenna operates in two frequency bands, 4.47-4.58 GHz and 5.08-5.22 GHz, and the return loss is -33.2 dB and - 22.6 dB at 4.52 GHz and 5.17 GHz, respectively, reaching a peak gain of 12.8 dBi. The proposed antenna shows low return loss and stable radiation direction map in the target frequency band. Ti3C2Tx MXene material is very suitable for the use of small-scale information transmission devices with the characteristics of high conductivity, weightless flexibility, and easy processing. The simulation results show the great potential of Ti3C2Tx MXene material as an RF device, which makes an significant exploration for the practical application of Ti3C2 devices in the antenna field.

articleTitle: Research on Broadband Multi-Channel Signal Processing Based on ADRV9009 and ZYNQ
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the rapid development of electronic information technology, in the fields of communication, radar, industrial automation, the measurement of multi-channel signal phase difference and signal amplitude measurement have higher requirements, so, can accurately measure the signal phase difference and amplitude, in theoretical research and practical engineering applications have very important significance. In order to meet the practical engineering requirements of fast, convenient and flexible signal measurement, this paper designs a small signal phase difference measurement and amplitude measurement equipment based on ADRV9009+ZYNQ. ADRV9009 is selected as the RF receiving chip, and the ZYNQ chip of Xilinx is used as the logic processing chip to design the minimum system circuit of ADRV9009. Finally, using the characteristics of In-phase Quadrature (IQ) signal, the calculation of signal phase difference and amplitude is completed by using the logical resources in ZYNQ. The feasibility of this scheme is verified in the hardware test platform, and it has strong engineering application value.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification Based on Dual-Channel Network with Spectral-Spatial Fusion Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) can extract intricate features from hyperspectral image (HSI) and demonstrate outstanding performance in HSI classification. However, as the depth of the CNN architectures expands, the size of the feature maps decreases, which can lead to the loss of some detail information and a decrease in resolution, ultimately leading to a deterioration in model performance. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a dual-channel network with spatial-spectral fusion attention (DC-SSFA). Firstly, the SSFA module aims to highlight important spectral spatial features and improve the network of utilization of global information in HSI. Secondly, to comprehensively extract the multi-scale feature information of HSI, the dual-branch fusion (DBF) module and the dilated convolutional fusion (DCF) module are proposed, and features with multiple receptive fields are fused to obtain different resolutions so as to enhance the representational capability of the dual-channel. Finally, residual module is introduced to realize the fusion of local and multi-scale information of HSI. Experiments are carried on three measured HSI datasets, compared with ClusterCNN, SSRN, HybridSN, and FC-3DCNN methods. The experimental results indicate that the DC-SSFA network provides promising classification performance.

articleTitle: Two-Axis Gimbal Motor Based on FPGA Control
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Two-axis gimbal is widely used in various industries, through the control of the motor in the gimbal to achieve the gimbal's attitude changes, the motor control directly affects the stability of the gimbal, accuracy and flexibility. However, most of the existing two-axis gimbal motor control Microcontroller Unit (MCU) as the main control, MCU needs to deal with complex algorithms and the face of the sensor data interaction, the system latency is large, the real-time response time of the gimbal becomes slower. To address these issues, this paper proposes a two-axis gimbal motor control on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), first of all, the overall control framework design, and then sub-module design and verify the correctness of the logic, and finally tested on the FPGA development board. The experimental results show that the gimbal motor has good control performance and fast response time.

articleTitle: The Simultaneous Localization and Mapping Technology for Intelligent Robots in Coal Mine Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To work underground in a coal mine, the first need to have a general understanding of the underground environment. However, there are many dangers in coal mines, such as gas explosions, mine collapses, etc. Therefore, robots can be used to replace humans for preliminary exploration of the underground environment in coal mines or even to perform tasks instead of humans. This approach can greatly reduce labor costs and effectively protect the safety of miners. But the underground environment of coal mines is usually complex, with numerous obstacles, winding passages, and other challenges. Traditional positioning methods, such as inertial navigation systems and Global Positioning System (GPS), have certain limitations and are difficult to use for accurate personnel positioning and map construction. This paper utilizes LiDAR Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technology to locate the robot itself and construct a map at the same time. An improved particle filter algorithm is employed to enhance the accuracy of robot positioning and mapping by optimizing the efficiency of resampling. Finally, experimental verification under simplified scenarios in MATLAB demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Emoji Recommendation Method Focusing on the Distribution of Emotion in the Context
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study performs sentiment analysis on tweets with emojis for an emoji recommendation model. Automatically collecting posts with emojis from social media, a dataset was assembled. Training was conducted on the WRIME dataset, which includes emotion intensity labels for social media texts, whereby a BERT-based sentiment classification model was used to analyze the emotion distribution of the context for each emoji in social media posts. This analysis determines which emoji is assigned to the text by the emotion distribution of the context, thereby handling complex sentiments expressed in different contexts, which is a more flexible emoji recommendation method than using the sentiment information of emojis alone. Experimental results showed that clustering emojis based on the emotion values of their context achieved the higher recommendation accuracy.

articleTitle: Human Action Recognition Based on Back Propagation Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study aims to explore the application of back propagation (BP) neural network technology to human action recognition. A human skeleton model is established based on joint nodes recognized with the Azure Kinect DK depth camera. The BP neural network model is then formulated and trained. With a relatively few training data, a group of carrying movements is recognized with high stability and accuracy. Compared with the traditional recognition based on images in pixel level, the human action recognition based on human skeleton model with BP neural network proved to be a reliable and efficient approach.

articleTitle: An Optimal Single Event Upset Mitigation Method for Programmable Logic in MPSoC
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To deal with single event upset phenomenon of configuration memory in on-orbit FPGA circuit, this paper proposes a multiple processors system on chip (MPSoC) with FPGA suitable method to single event upset recovery. This method uses the PCAP interface of the SoC architecture to realize the SEU caused error detection of the configuration data by the processor using the readback comparison without affecting the normal operation of the FPGA functional circuit. Finally, the fault injection experiment is carried out by SEM IP, which verifies the effectiveness of the configuration data SEU detection recovery method in both directions, and evaluates the speed advantage of the recovery method according to the average fault recovery response time.

articleTitle: Research on Printing Icons Defect Detection Based on Variation Model Consistent with Subjective Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of existing detection methods for printing icons on glass bottles in industrial production lines, a defect detection method for printing icons based on an improved variation model is proposed. On the basis of using variation model to detect bottle icons, subjective evaluation standards are introduced from both model training and comparison, and a locally variable variation model is constructed to improve the problems existing in the basic model. The experimental results show that compared with existing methods, the research method proposed in this paper is more feasible in practical detection, and the results are more in line with the subjective validity of detection. It can better detect bottle icons judged as defects in actual production lines.

articleTitle: SOC+FPGA High Speed SDIO Interface Design
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The purpose of this design is to design a high-speed interface to realize high-speed communication between rv1106 chip and FPGA. The processor in rv1106 can process complex logic circuits, but the processing speed is not high, while FPGA can improve the speed although the processing logic is simple, and the combination of the two can process complex logic at high speed [7]. After comprehensive consideration, the SDIO(Secure Digital Input and Output) communication interface [3] is used. The SDIO interface is an interface developed on the basis of the interface of SD memory card, which can provide high-speed transmission interface for the chip.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph Construction Method for Complex Products Improvement Design
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Nowadays, complex products play a key role in fields such as industrial engineering and smart manufacturing, and their improved design is crucial in reducing maintenance costs and enhancing product performance and reliability. However, due to the extreme complexity of heterogeneous data in the product life cycle, the field of complex products improvement design still lacks a unified knowledge representation framework. Aiming to fulfill the gap, knowledge graph (KG) is introduced as a powerful tool for managing intricate system knowledge. By collecting multisource and heterogeneous data across the life cycle and conducting knowledge extraction, design knowledge and related historical knowledge are processed and represented into a unified form through function-behavior-structure (FBS) model. Finally, a KG is constructed under the guidance of ontology to provide a knowledge basis for tasks such as knowledge reuse and solution recommendation in the field of complex products improvement design.

articleTitle: Using Multi-Objective Optimization for Enhancing Generalization in Symbolic Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: An essential feature of a symbolic regression problem is the ability to generalize a function model. If the data samples are overfit, the model's capacity to generalize may be reduced. It is worth the effort to figure out how to improve the learning model's generalization while maintaining learning precision. This work suggested a multi-objective optimization strategy to improve the learning model's generalization, based on the structural risk reduction concept. Two optimization objectives were identified: empirical risk and confidence risk. Integrated learning techniques were applied to the Pareto optimal solutions obtained through Gene Expression Programming (GEP) to generate a final function model with enhanced fitting precision and generalization capabilities. articleTitle: Transformer Fault Knowledge Map Recommendation Algorithm Based on Intelligent Assistant
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To solve the problem of transformer fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a transformer fault recommendation algorithm based on knowledge graph: the triplet in knowledge graph is transformed into a word vector according to the word embedding transformation method, and then the word vector is initialized, and the transformer components, fault types and phenomena are associated according to the distance translation model, and the confidence is obtained. The auxiliary push part assigns the weight according to the severity of the result caused by the transformer fault, and adjusts the proportion of the severity of the fault in the recommended result according to the range mapping to obtain the recommended proportion coefficient. When a fault is queried, the knowledge with high confidence is returned. If the fault is queried for the first time, the proportional weighting is recommended. Otherwise, the linear weighting is performed based on the historical query results to obtain the final output result. Through simulation, the AUC index of the model is close to 0.9, and the first three pushed can basically cover the failure and reduce the economic loss.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Anomaly Detection Based on Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network and Gated Recurrent Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Detection of abnormal network traffic is crucial for network security, and existing methods often require a substantial amount of abnormal network traffic for effective detection. However, in most cases, samples of abnormal network traffic are imbalanced, posing a challenge for effective detection. This paper proposes a method for detecting imbalanced network traffic anomalies by combining WGAN and GRU. The approach involves sampling the network traffic dataset, balancing the imbalanced dataset using WGAN, and inputting the balanced network traffic data into GRU for prediction. The UNSW-NB15 network intrusion detection dataset was used for testing, and results show that the model achieves high accuracy in detecting imbalanced abnormal network traffic.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Gravity Minimum Support Regularization Inversion Combined with Prior Image Information
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In a geophysical inversion, forms of prior information are various. However, it is not easy to obtain prior lithologic or structural information. In order to integrate image information into the geophysical inversion, this paper takes the 3D gravity regularization inversion as an example, integrates prior image information into a minimum support stabilizer, and proposes a new stabilizer. Then, single-block and double-block model tests are designed and implemented. Compared with the result using the minimum support stabilizer, the result of using the new stabilizer can better restores the lithologic and structural distribution of underground anomaly. Besides, the resolution of the gravity method is improved. It can be concluded that the new stabilizer is suitable for 3D gravity inversion, providing a new idea for the integration of prior information in geophysical inversion.

articleTitle: Design of a 20-to-40 GHz Millimetre-Wave Ultra-Wideband Low Noise Amplifier in 55-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper describes a broadband millimeter-wave LNA for multi-band applications. In order to minimize noise and maximize gain, an innovative amplifier architecture is introduced, which combine the triple-coupled transformer technique with a Gm-boosting type common source and common gate amplification structure is proposed. In addition, this paper employs a multi-resonant cavity-type matching network as the input impedance matching network, an L-type structure as the interstage matching network, and a T-type structure as the output impedance matching network. The circuit's bandwidth has been significantly enhanced through an excellent design methodology. This low noise amplifier is built and simulated with 55-nm CMOS process. The simulation results demonstrate that the circuit achieving a peak gain of 21.68 dB and the 3dB gain bandwidth up to 20 GHz. Over the entire operating bandwidth, the noise figure ranging between 3.5-3.7 dB. Furthermore, the input 1 dB compression point is -21.17 dBm.

articleTitle: Product Qulity Traceability of Cold Chain Logistics Based on Multimodal Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Cold chain logistics product quality traceability(CCLPQT) plays a crucial role in ensuring food safety and enhancing consumer trust, especially for products that require specific temperature and humidity conditions under varying environments. However, traditional quality traceability methods use inadequate data sources and neglect the use of heterogeneous data from multiple sources, which has present several challenges in cold chain logistics product quality traceability. One significant challenge is how to accurately capture, integrate, and utilize heterogeneous data from multiple sources to determine product quality status in a real-time manner. To address this challenge, a multi-modal knowledge graph-based method for cold chain logistics product quality traceability is proposed. By acquiring and integrating real-time text data, image data, and temperature and humidity data, a multi-modal knowledge graph for CCLPQT is established. Consequently, the real-time monitoring of product quality status at different stages (e.g., storage, transportation, sale, etc.), the visualization of data, and the efficient coordination of quality traceability activities can be achieved.

articleTitle: A Rapid Training Method for Color Correction Models in Machine Vision Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: When using machine vision systems to replace human eyes for color difference detection of products, machine vision systems are greatly affected by hardware and environmental conditions. When one or more factors change, it often reduces the accuracy of machine vision systems for color difference detection. The traditional sample collection method has a complex process and takes a long time. If samples are customized based on the hardware configuration and environmental conditions of the system, the cost is high and the generalization is poor. To address these issues, this article proposes a rapid training scheme. This scheme adds a compensation model to the basic model of color correction in the machine vision system, uses polynomial regression to correct the collected colors, and tests the results. The experimental results show that after changes in device and environmental conditions, the accuracy and performance of the rapid training color correction model are higher than those of the Initial color correction model.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Stabilization for a Class of Nonlinear Systems with Sampled and Inaccurate Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper addresses the stabilization problem for the lower-triangular nonlinear systems via output feedback. Based on the inaccurate output measurements, a truncation protocol is adopted and then a continuous state observer without output measurements and a discontinuous control law are designed. The network-induced delay is also taken into consideration. Then, some sufficient conditions and a bound of delay are derived to ensure that the system states could be stabilized to a bounded region.

articleTitle: An Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm Based Computer Unified Device Architecture to Symbolic Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Symbolic regression, as a data-driven function modeling method based on evolutionary computation, is widely applied in many fields. For scenarios that require real-time modeling, the timeliness of the algorithm becomes particularly important. This paper proposes a parallel computing approach utilizing the computational power of GPUs to parallelize the particle swarm optimization algorithm for solving symbolic regression problems. By introducing and Scatter operator and mutation operator and a hierarchical self-adaptive learning strategy of particles, the local exploration and global search capabilities of particles are enhanced to improve the efficiency of the algorithm. Numerical experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an acceleration ratio of approximately 20 times compared to running on a CPU, and the acceleration effect becomes more evident with the increase of the data scale.

articleTitle: Prediction of Regional Truck Traffic Status Based on GPS Data
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study introduces a novel model employing GRU (Gated Unit Neural Network) and APSO (Adaptive Nonlinear Inertial Weighted Particle Swarm Optimization) for forecasting truck traffic status. Initially, principles for data cleaning are established to address five types of abnormal data from truck GPS. Subsequently, the APSO algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the GRU network for improved performance and efficiency, resulting in the development of an APSO-GRU regional truck traffic state prediction model. Finally, multiscenario numerical simulations illustrate improved prediction accuracy compared to GRU, SVR (Support Vector Regression), and ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model).

articleTitle: Calculating Dual Integration with a Triple Integral Calculator
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In response to the problem that the existing triple integral calculator is unable to calculate the double integral, this paper improves the triple integral calculator. Firstly, the input modes for users to calculate the dual and triple integrals are introduced respectively. Secondly, a method is designed to transform the dual integral input mode into an equivalent triple integral input mode. Finally, the method of calculating the dual integral with the triple integral calculator is designed. The experimental results show that the improved triple integral calculator is capable of calculating double integrals.

articleTitle: Correlation Matching Method for Speech Signals at Different Sampling Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Aiming to the problem of determining the signal source of speech signals with different sampling rates, a method is proposed to match speech signals with different sampling rates. This method performs bilinear interpolation on the speech signal with the smaller sampling rate to transform its sampling rate, making the sampling rates of the two digital speech signals approximately equal. Then, it calculates the cross-correlation function of the two digital speech signals. Based on the observation of significant correlation peaks, it calculates the peak-to-mean ratio of the cross-correlation function and the sliding correlation coefficient to determine if the speech signals are from the same source. Simulation results show that this method can effectively determine whether two speech signals with different sampling rates belong to the same speech signal source.

articleTitle: Cricket Action Classification Based on Skeleton Data Extracted by OpenPifPaf
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study explores the classification of cricket actions using a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), based on skeleton keypoint data. Our research demonstrates the capability of GCN to significantly outperform traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in analyzing complex spatial relationships inherent in skeletal data. The GCN achieved an 85% accuracy in classifying various cricket actions such as batting, bowling, catching, and fielding, compared to the 60% accuracy obtained with a conventional CNN approach. These findings highlight the potential of applying advanced graph-based neural networks in sports analytics and suggest further applicability in real-time performance monitoring and training enhancements. This work lays the groundwork for future exploration into diverse applications of graph neural networks in sports science and other areas involving intricate data relationships.

articleTitle: Study on the Iterative Estimation and Compensation Algorithm for IQ Imbalance in Coherent Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Coherent optical communication technology is a key technology for building high-speed optical fibre communication networks, while the amplitude and phase imbalance between the in-phase and quadrature (IQ) signals at the receiving end will lead to the degradation of the received signal quality and affect the performance of the communication system. In this thesis, a narrowband zero-intermediate frequency (ZIF) receiver IQ imbalance estimation and compensation algorithm is proposed with the research objective of designing IQ imbalance estimation and compensation algorithms for the 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (16QAM) signal in coherent optical communication systems that can be implemented in hardware circuits. The algorithm is based on the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization procedure (GSOP) for approximate estimation of the IQ imbalance parameters and improves the estimation accuracy of the IQ imbalance parameters by means of iterative optimization. The IQ imbalance signal is effectively compensated by the inverse matrix of the IQ mismatch parameter matrix. Based on the estimation error of the IQ imbalance parameters, the bit error rate (BER) of the signal transmission at different signal to noise ratio (SNR), and the simulation results of the 16QAM constellation diagram before and after compensation, it is concluded that the iterative optimized algorithm based on GSOP reduces the complexity of hardware implementation and improves the efficiency and accuracy of the IQ imbalance parameters estimation effectively. The findings of this study hold practical engineering significance for estimating and calibrating IQ imbalance in coherent optical communication systems using high-order modulated signals through digital signal processing techniques.

articleTitle: Study on Sensor Layout Method Based on Mutual Information
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The diffusion of toxic gas caused by the leakage of stored high-pressure chemical gases will cause significant harm to the environment and residents. Therefore, it is crucial to trace the source of leakage and predict the dispersion range of leakage accidents quickly. When using diffusion models to predict poisonous gas leaks, errors are accumulated due to the influence of meteorological, terrain and other factors, which affects the prediction accuracy, Therefore, sensors need to be deployed to use the data captured as observation value to correct models. However, the high cost of arranging and maintaining toxic gas sensors makes it difficult to place a large number of them, so how to place a limited number of sensors in the optimal location is a hot research issue. In this paper, we propose a sensor optimization layout strategy based on the gradient of mutual information, which utilizes the mutual information between the concentration of poisonous gas and the release source at the detection location as an indicator, and avoids traversing the search to improve the search efficiency through the gradient-based sequence forward selection search strategy. The time complexity is reduced from O(n2) to O(n),and at the same time, comparative experiments are conducted with other optimization algorithms, which show that the gradient-based forward selection search strategy is similar to other optimization algorithms in terms of time spent, and is more accurate in terms of convergence than other optimization algorithms

articleTitle: A University Sports Performance Prediction Model Based on Improved Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Addressing the issues of the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) being prone to local optima and lacking in global search capability, this study employs a Circle chaotic sequence to initialize the population individuals, ensuring an even distribution of initial population individuals. An adaptive position update strategy is utilized to enhance the algorithm's global search capability, while a reverse search strategy is employed to expand the search space and prevent falling into local optima. The Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer algorithm is used to optimize the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model for predicting college student sports performance, and comparative analyses are conducted with other prediction algorithms. Results indicate that the proposed prediction model demonstrates superior predictive accuracy and applicability in forecasting college student sports performance.

Author Keywords: Grey Wolf Algorithm Grey Wolf Algorithm

articleTitle: Single Image Deraining Based on Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To address the challenges of prolonged sampling time and the limitation to process specific image sizes in current image deraining research, we propose a novel single image deraining approach based on denoising diffusion implicit models. The method adopts a variant of the U-Net fully convolutional network architecture based on SR3, concatenating rainy images of arbi-trary sizes and noise images along the channel dimension to iteratively obtain high-resolution rain-free images. Specifically, we in-corporate residual blocks from BigGAN-deep to replace traditional residual blocks, thereby deepening the network to enhance model generalization. Additionally, we employ smooth noise esti-mation via image overlapping block processing to improve image fidelity. Introducing deterministic acceleration sampling, we expe-dite the sampling process by uniformly selecting time steps. Comprehensive testing on synthetic and real datasets demonstrates that the proposed method achieves deraining for images of any size, yielding significant improvements in peak signal-to-noise ra-tio and structural similarity. The generated images preserve more complete details, showing superior deraining efficacy.

articleTitle: Optimization of Weighted KNN Algorithm Based on Transition Probability
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In addressing diverse data types, the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm displays pronounced variability in accuracy. Determining the optimal range for the number of adjacent sample points, k, and their associated weights presents significant challenges. This paper proposes an optimized KNN method, termed TPW-KNN, which dynamically selects the range of neighboring samples through transition probability and computes weights using the Kriging equation. Compared to traditional weighted KNN methods, the TPW-KNN algorithm exhibits superior generalizability and classification performance, effectively mitigating the influence of data characteristics such as varying sample densities and the complexities involved in classifying small datasets.

articleTitle: Data Recovery Method for Truncated Gzip Compressed Files
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Data recovery for truncated gzip compressed files is a critical task in various industries and open-source communities where gzip compression is widely utilized for its efficiency in reducing file sizes while maintaining data integrity. This paper presents a method of data recovery for truncated gzip compressed files, focusing on the principles, implementation, efficiency, and implications of such a method. The first part of the paper provides an in-depth introduction to the gzip file format and the binary construction of gzip files is outlined. The second part of the paper introduces a principle-based approach to data recovery for truncated gzip compressed files, which involves iteratively removing extraneous bits from the beginning of the truncated file until a complete DEFLATE block is obtained, enabling successful decoding of the file. Implementation details of this approach, including the iterative decoding process and its impact on data recovery efficiency, are discussed in detail. The third part of the paper evaluates the efficiency of the data recovery method, focusing on the impact of DEFLATE block size and the iterative decoding process. Smaller DEFLATE blocks are found to facilitate quick data recovery, while the iterative decoding process incrementally narrows down the search space for the first complete DEFLATE block. Tradeoffs and considerations associated with the iterative decoding process are also discussed, highlighting the importance of ongoing research and development efforts to further improve data recovery efficiency. By leveraging principles of the gzip file format and DEFLATE compression, it is possible to develop effective data recovery techniques that can recover significant portions of the original uncompressed data from truncated gzip compressed files.

articleTitle: Application of Untracked Particle Filter (PSO-UPF) Based on Particle Swarm Optimization in Indoor Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To address the issue of particle depletion caused by resampling in traditional particle filter algorithms, an unscented particle filter algorithm (PSO-UPF) based on particle swarm optimization is proposed to enhance the number of particles and improve estimation accuracy. The study first examines the principles and implementation process of the particle swarm optimization algorithm, then compares the similarities and differences between particle swarm optimization and particle filter algorithms, focusing on how particle swarm optimization can alleviate the particle depletion problem. The effect of each particle is improved, and the basic steps of PSO-UPF algorithm are given. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the system's robustness, real-time performance and effectiveness of the system compared with PF, UPF and PSO-PF.

articleTitle: Steel Surface Defect Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: There are some defects on the surface of steel that are difficult to detect, so we propose an improved algorithm based on YOLOv8 for detecting defects that are difficult to be detected. This improvement includes the introduction of an SPD module to minimize the problem of information loss due to downsampling; the addition of a small object detection head combined with EMA attention to further enhance the detection capabilities for small targets; the use of BiFPN to replace the original PANet, applying different weights to different features to strengthen feature fusion. Experiments were conducted on the NEU-DET dataset, and the algorithm improved mAP to 80.2%, an improvement of 3.9% over the baseline model.

articleTitle: Detection and Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease Using Fundus Images with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Early detection and risk prediction of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) would help reduce CVD-related complications and lessen their impact on a global scale. Cost-effective, noninvasive retinal fundus imaging can be used alongside deep learning to assist with early detection and risk prediction during routine eye exams that most individuals have on a yearly basis. In this paper, deep learning methods are tested for CVD detection and risk prediction using fundus images as the sole source of data due to medical information not always being readily available for all patients. The proposed methods will be implemented utilizing convolutional neural networks(CNNs) and transfer learning. The results and a comparison between different transfer learning models will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Interactive Emotional Learning in Emotional Intelligent Dialogue Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence in the field of conversational systems, users have raised higher demands for the emotional expression capabilities of dialogue agents. To address this issue, we proposed an Interactional Emotional Learning model (TIEL) tailored for task-oriented dialogue, aimed at enhancing the emotional prediction accuracy of dialogue agents and addressing the issue of missing target text. The TIEL model achieved a deep understanding of multi-turn dialogue contexts and accurate prediction of emotional categories through three modules: knowledge-enhanced dialogue context encoding, latent emotional response learning, and interactive emotional prediction. Experimental results on the DailyDialog dataset demonstrated a significant performance improvement of the TIEL model in emotion prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Simulation Platform for Fault Injection to Configuration Bitstream based on Multiple Cores Architecture Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The large scale digital circuit in space radiation is susceptible to single event upset caused by single event effect. It is particularly important to reinforce the FPGA from the perspective of reliability. The cost of conducting real irradiation experiments is too high and too expensive. Therefore, this paper proposes a SEM IP core based method to design an experimental and verification platform for simulating single event upset. This method performs bit-by-bit fault injection on the configuration bits in the user memory through SEM IP, and reads back to judge the consistency to verify the correctness of the method. The results show that the platform can inject faults accurately and quickly to meet the requirements of simulating space environment.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Vision Transformer Model for Image Recognition in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Large-scale vision models have achieved significant results across various tasks, including image segmentation, image classification, object detection. However, due to the variations in resolution, object scales, shapes, and textures inherent in power images, the application of large-scale vision models in the power domain remains to be further explored. In this paper, we proposed a Large-Scale Vision Transformer model (LSVT) based on an advancing plain vision transformers (Vits) for power system image recognition. The model employs a rotated varied-size attention (RVSA) mechanism, which enables more efficient and accurate handling of task objects that vary in size, shape, and texture. Experimental results demonstrate that our model has attained remarkable performance in the power domain, achieving an average precision of 82.56% for object detection task and 88.43% average accuracy for image classification task on a power image dataset.

articleTitle: A Robust Deep Learning Framework for Ovarian Cancer Subtype Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Accurate identification of ovarian cancer subtypes from histopathological images is crucial for guiding treatment, but remains challenging. We present a deep learning approach to classify ovarian cancer subtypes from whole slide images (WSIs) and tissue microarrays (TMAs). Our EfficientNetV2 based model achieved 93.08% balanced accuracy on WSIs, outperforming prior methods. To enable TMA inference, we developed an algorithm to generate a TMA-like dataset from WSIs, allowing our model to achieve 80% accuracy on a true TMA test set. This highlights the robustness and clinical potential of our framework for aiding ovarian cancer diagnosis and treatment selection.

articleTitle: Deeply Reforming the Economic and Carbon Assessment of Building Energy Consumption in the Block System
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Reducing building energy consumption is crucial in the face of global warming and resource depletion challenges. As the fundamental unit of a city, neighborhoods contain enormous potential for carbon reduction in all aspects. By drawing inspiration from the overall renovation of the neighborhood system and deeply optimizing the systems of buildings, energy supply, production capacity, carbon sequestration, etc. we can explore more efficient technological paths, improve energy utilization efficiency, and inject new vitality into the sustainable development of the city. The block renovation project not only helps promote sustainable development, but also improves the living environment and enhances community well-being. The retrofitting measures have effectively improved energy efficiency. The energy consumption of the building is estimated to have been reduced by 17%, and the overall carbon emissions have been significantly reduced, reaching an annual reduction of 5,339.777 tonnes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> equivalent, carbon emissions from energy supply and production systems were reduced by 5250 tons of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> per year, those from greening systems by 63.93 tons of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> per year and those from the convenience system (where electric bikes are placed at fence removal sites) by about 148 tons of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> per year. At the same time, the residents' life satisfaction and the quality of living environment have also improved.

articleTitle: MPSoC Based Smart Read-Back and Scrubbing Mechanism for FPGA with Frame Granularity
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To protect the single event upset of FPGA logic circuits caused by radiation in outer space, especially the upset of configuration memory, this paper proposes a FPGA single event upset detection mechanism on frame level granularity for multiple core processor system on chip (MPSoC). This mechanism smartly adopts the PCAP interface of SoC architecture to garden the basic bits related to configuration under the condition that the whole system function of FPGA works normally. The processor system contentiously reads back frame by frame for SEU error detection, and if errors found, MPSoC will scrub the right frame where error located. The method could adaptive migrate the error frame when needed, and as a result it is expected to correct SEU more effectively.

articleTitle: Compressive Sensing-Based OTFS Channel Estimation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation technology effectively addresses the issue of information transmission under high-speed motion conditions. Its channel within the delay-Doppler domain exhibits sparsity, making it feasible to employ compressive sensing algorithms for OTFS channel estimation. Traditional greedy iterative compressive sensing based channel estimation algorithms require sparsity as a prior condition. However, obtaining sparsity in practical scenarios is often challenging, potentially leading to decreased performance. A channel estimation algorithm that integrates wavelet threshold denoising with compressive sensing theory is proposed which adjusts the threshold parameters of the reconstruction algorithm based on the estimation of the noise standard deviation in the channel. Moreover, it utilizes the denoised channel response as the termination condition for the reconstruction algorithm iterations, achieving adaptive sparsity reconstruction of the channel response. Simulation results indicate that under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, the proposed algorithm improves estimation performance by approximately 3 dB compared to the traditional segmented weak orthogonal matching pursuit algorithms, with only a slight increase in algorithm complexity.

articleTitle: Loop Unrolling Based on SLP and Register Pressure Awareness
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Loop unrolling is a common compiler optimization technique that reduces the execution count of loop branch instructions and improves program performance by merging multiple iterations of a loop body into a single iteration. In LLVM, the native loop unrolling model considers only the impact of the number of instructions within the loop body when computing the unrolling factor, without accounting for subsequent optimizations and register resources. To address this issue, a new loop unrolling model is proposed that takes into account subsequent superword level parallelism (SLP) vectorization and register pressure. When computing the unrolling factor, the model uses the benefit for SLP (BSLP) model to identify loops that can be vectorized by SLP after loop unrolling and calculates the unrolling factor to support subsequent SLP vectorization. The register pressure-aware loop unrolling (RPLU) model adjusts the unrolling factor to mitigate excessive register pressure, thereby reducing the impact of register spills. Experimental results show that, compared to the loop unrolling model in LLVM, this model can compute more effective loop unrolling factors and improve program performance. The average speedup on the SPEC CPU 2006 benchmark suite is 2.0%, with a maximum speedup of 5.1%, and the average speedup on the TSVC benchmark suite is 5.1%, with a maximum speedup of 34.4%.

articleTitle: A Subway Passenger Flow Prediction Based on Long Short-Term Memory Combined with Seasonal and Trend Decomposition Using Loess Algorithm and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Accurate and real-time prediction of subway passenger flow is very important for the transportation department. Due to the obvious fluctuation of subway passenger flow, it is crucial to enhance the reliability of subway traffic flow projections, this paper proposes an STL algorithm and genetic algorithm to optimize the LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) prediction model STL-GaLSTM. First, the STL method decomposes the dataset into three variables that exhibit robust regularity, thereby increasing the input dimensionality. Secondly, a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the LSTM model, primarily focusing on refining the number of LSTM layers and the number of neurons within the hidden layers, to determine the optimal parameter combination, and to use the optimized LSTM to train and predict the model on the data set processed by STL algorithm. The test results show that the proposed prediction model has greatly improved the prediction accuracy of subway passenger flow. The STL and genetic algorithms are effective at capturing the dynamic characteristics of data, thereby providing a more accurate prediction of subway commuter volumes.

articleTitle: Research on Fast Location of WKNN Indoor WiFi Fingerprint Based on Double Search
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In order to reduce the influence of Wi-Fi signal fluctuation on the positioning accuracy, this paper improves the Wi-Fi fingerprint positioning algorithm by variational mode decomposition (VMD), and uses VMD to smooth the noise while maintaining the original characteristics of the signal. In order to solve the problem of low real-time positioning of WKNN algorithm when dealing with a large number of fingerprint data, this paper constructs a guide database and a target database, optimizes their data structures by using ball-tree, and realizes a two-way fast search mechanism by using multi-thread parallel processing. On the premise of ensuring the matching accuracy, the matching number of fingerprint points in the positioning process is effectively reduced and the positioning efficiency is accelerated. The data collected by esp8266 Wi-Fi signal collector designed by ourselves in real environment shows that the positioning accuracy and speed of this method are improved by about 20% and 40% respectively compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: BiKD-Yolo: A Small Object Detection Algorithm from UAV Perspective Based on BiFormer Attention and Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Object detection is crucial for the real-time operations of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), particularly in identifying small objects within UAV imagery. While existing computer vision techniques have shown success in UAV applications, detecting small objects remains challenging due to limited information, small size, and low resolution. This study presents the BiKD-YOLO approach, which combines BiFormer attention and knowledge distillation to enhance both the precision and efficiency of small object detection. We employ SAHI (Slice-Assisted Hyper-Inference) cropping to enlarge small objects in images, followed by knowledge distillation for model compression, facilitating knowledge transfer from larger to smaller models for streamlined operation. Through the incorporation of the BiFormer attention mechanism, the detection process is further refined by focusing on critical regions of interest, thereby improving overall accuracy. Experimental Results from tests on the VisDrone dataset show that BiKD-Yolo greatly surpasses the baseline, delivering superior performance in detection accuracy, mAP, and AP metrics. In summary, the BiKD-Yolo method presents a novel and effective solution for improving small object detection in UAV images, offering enhanced accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Generative Adversarial Network for Artistic Style Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Currently, image style transfer is one of the hotspots in image processing. Generative adversarial networks have been successfully applied in many fields by virtue of their advantages, and the technology of image style transfer has also seen improvements. However, there are still some problems with the existing artistic style transfer models. For example, the generated images will contain noisy textures, the style and color effects are not ideal, and the model has many parameters, which is easy to cause model breakdown and unstable training. To overcome these problems, an image transfer method that improves the cycleconsistent generative adversarial network (CycleGAN) is presented in this paper. According to its structural characteristics, distributed shift convolution (DSConv) is introduced through the quantized neural network, and the reverse residual block is used to optimize the generator network structure, which can greatly reduce the calculation amount of the model while also improving the model's perception ability and accuracy and the quality of the generated images. Experiments show that the proposed approach can improve the content details of the generated image andthe color effect of the style texture, significantly reduces the number of model parameters, reduces the computational cost, improves the transfer rate, upgrading the model performance, and has strong style transfer capabilities.

articleTitle: Indoor and Outdoor Scene Classification Method Based on Improved Shared K -Nearest Neighbor
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In view of the problems of insufficient classification accuracy, low reliability and poor stability of current indoor and outdoor scene recognition methods, a method of indoor and outdoor scene classification based on improved shared K-nearest neighbors was proposed. The method makes full use of WiFi Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), number of visible satellites and Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) The different characteristics displayed in indoor and outdoor environments enable effective scene identification. Firstly, K adjacent points with the highest similarity were selected by calculating the category belonging degree between the points to be classified and the classified samples. Secondly, the sample that is most similar to the point to be classified is identified, and K classified nearest neighbors of the sample are determined. Finally, the improved shared K-neighbor algorithm is used to calculate the number of shared neighbors between the points to be classified and the most similar points, and according to the indoor and outdoor category belonging degree and size of these shared neighbors, the prediction category of the points to be classified is used to achieve the final classification of the classification points. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional classification methods K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), random forest, decision tree, C4.5 decision tree and Naive Bayesian Model (NBM), the classification accuracy of indoor and outdoor scenes is improved by 1.5%, 9%, 9.5% and 1 % respectively.

articleTitle: Consistency of Clustering Between Optimal Fuzzy Equivalence Relation and C-Means
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In cluster analysis, there are two important kinds of fuzzy clustering methods. One is fuzzy C-means clustering, in which the model proposed by Bezdek is a typical representative. Another kind is the clustering based on similarity relations, such as transitive closure method. What is the inherent connection between the two kinds of clustering methods? This paper studies this problem based on their two representative models. Through theoretical analyses and a case test it finds that they are consistent in cluster analysis. This not only enriches clustering theory, but also has practical value. In addition, this paper also makes some discussions on the clustering based on similarity relations, in order to make the methods of this kind better applied to cluster analysis.

articleTitle: Fast Fourier Transform Improved Frequency Offset Estimation Algorithm in Coherent Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Frequency offset estimation is an important part of digital signal processing (DSP), and its estimation performance is the key factor of signal demodulation. To improve the estimation accuracy of frequency offset estimation algorithm and reduce the hardware implementation complexity of the algorithm, this paper proposes a blind frequency offset estimation combining multi-level iterative fast Fourier transform (FFT) and fence effect estimation. Simulation experiments show that under the same simulation conditions in a 16QAM coherent optical communication system, compared with several traditional algorithms, the estimated mean square error of this algorithm is reduced by 4 orders of magnitude, and the computational complexity is reduced by about 70 times.

articleTitle: A Comparison Study in Detecting Knee Osteoarthritis Severity with Deep Leaning
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (Knee OA or KOA) presents a significant medical challenge due to its prevalence and the complexities involved in diagnosis. Manual diagnosis of KOA is time-consuming and susceptible to errors, particularly considering that a majority (60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) of Knee OA cases occur in elderly individuals. Thus, the development of an accurate and reliable diagnostic system is imperative. Deep neural network (DNN) models offer a promising avenue for automating the identification and classification of Knee OA images. Leveraging their capability to discern intricate patterns within images, DNNs facilitate a comprehensive analysis of KOA images. In this study, we conduct a comparison study in diagnosing Knee OA with two different datasets. We employ several DNN models including Custom CNN, ResNet101, EfficientNet, and ConvNextBase, assessing their performance on a withheld test dataset. Our proposed approach stands to revolutionize the diagnosis of Knee OA, offering potential benefits such as enhanced diagnostic accuracy and the prospect of early detection. Early diagnosis facilitated by this method holds the promise of prompt intervention, thereby mitigating the progression of knee joint damage. Overall, ConvNeXtBase performs the best in our comparison study.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Circularly Polarised Antenna with Parasitic Branches
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband circularly polarised antenna loaded with short and long parasitic branches for K-band applications. In order to satisfy the demand for broadband in communication systems, the antenna is connected to a rectangular patch radiating unit with a rectangular slot ground plane to generate K-band radiation, and the antenna is circularly polarised by loading parasitic dendrites to break the current equilibrium. The results show that the antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth coverage of 23% (21.3-26.8 GHz), a 3dB axial ratio bandwidth coverage of 34.5% (21.3-29.6 GHz), and a peak gain of 9.4dBi at 24 GHz, which is in line with the expected band design requirements. The antenna achieves ultra-wideband performance and excellent circular polarisation performance, and exhibits excellent performance in K-band, providing an important solution for applications in wireless communications and radar, among others, and is of reference significance.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation with Alternate Guidance from Multiple Teachers
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In unsupervised domain adaptive semantic segmentation, the Mean Teacher framework has demonstrated strong performance. By utilizing two models with the same structure but different initializations, it effectively leverages unlabeled data to train the model. However, in this framework, the Teacher Model's (T-Model) parameters are updated as the exponential moving average (EMA) of the Student Model's (S-Model). This update mechanism heavily relies on the S-Model and may reinforce erroneous knowledge if the S-Model learns incorrect information. We propose an Alternating Guidance from Multiple Teachers (AGMT) method to address the issues inherent in the Mean Teacher framework. Our approach involves initializing three T-Models with the same network but different parameters at the start of training. During training, these T-Models are dynamically activated in an alternating manner to guide the training of the S-Model. Moreover, we introduce correlation-mixed sampling and boundary sampling techniques, which help the model learn better boundary features, thereby improving segmentation accuracy for rare classes.

articleTitle: Adaptive Flight Control Based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the increasing demand for intelligent and automated inspection in the power industry, the importance of drones as efficient and flexible inspection tools is becoming increasingly prominent. However, traditional flight control methods lack intelligence and cannot effectively cope with the current complex and ever-changing power inspection scenarios. Therefore, this article proposes an adaptive flight control method based on artificial intelligence. Firstly, build an intelligent PID controller based on deep neural networks, and then use this controller to provide real-time and accurate feedback adjustment of PID parameters, achieving adaptive adjustment and optimization control of drone flight, ensuring stable and efficient performance of the drone in different flight scenarios. In the scenario of power inspection, the adaptive flight control method based on artificial intelligence can not only significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of inspection, but also reduce the risk and cost of human operation.

articleTitle: Research on Wheat Ear Recognition Method Based on Image Color Features and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In this paper, we study wheat images during the grouting period, and construct a dataset by extracting wheat spike features through image preprocessing, color space conversion and edge detection. Convolutional Neural Network and AlexNet models are used to train and optimize the parameters and structure to improve the recognition accuracy. By adjusting the batch size, learning rate and training rounds, CNN performs optimally with Batch size=64, Epoch=5, and learning rate=0.001; AlexNet also performs well with similar settings, but the training cost is larger. This study verifies the effectiveness of image processing combined with the classical model CNN for recognizing wheat sheaves, providing data and theoretical support for wheat yield prediction.

articleTitle: Self-Knowledge Distillation Method Using Adaptive Mixed Attention for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Model compression using self-knowledge distillation methods has achieved remarkable performance in tasks such as image classification and object detection. However, most current self-knowledge distillation approaches focus on the foreground of the image, overlooking background knowledge, while their attention mechanisms may also focus wrong, leading to the omission of vital subject knowledge. This paper addresses these issues by proposing a self-knowledge distillation method based on an adaptive mixed attention mechanism. The adaptive mixed attention mechanism adjusts attention according to feature maps of the image, allowing for the rational extraction of both foreground and background knowledge. This enhancement improves the accuracy and stability of knowledge extraction, thereby boosting the precision of image classification. Experimental results demonstrate that the method using the ResNet34 network achieves accuracy improvements of 2.48% on the CIFAR100 dataset and 1.21% on the Tiny-ImageNet dataset. For fine-grained visual recognition tasks, the method using the ResNet34 network improves accuracy by 3.69% on the CUB200 dataset and 1.43% on the MIT67 dataset, respectively.

articleTitle: Intelligent Collaborative Driving Lane Changing Decision of Multi-Intelligent Connected Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study proposes a multi intelligent connected vehicles (ICV) collaborative lane changing model based on Deep Q-Networks (DQN), and verifies its effectiveness in dynamic traffic environment through the test of highway-env simulation environment. The results show that with the increase of training times, the model can significantly improve the overall average speed of the team. Further analysis shows that the model shows different performance under different traffic density and the number of controlled vehicles. The research shows that when the density continues to increase, the reward value, average speed and headway of intelligent connected vehicles all show a downward trend. In addition, when the number of controlled vehicles increases from 3 to 5, although the average reward value and headway of the fleet increase, the average speed decreases. This study provides a new perspective and method for the optimization of vehicle collaborative behavior and the improvement of traffic efficiency in intelligent transportation system.

articleTitle: Industrial Discharge Detection Based on Improved U-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The probability of industrial production accidents (such as harmful gas leaks, fires, explosions) is very low, and there are very few abnormal samples. Traditional anomaly detection methods require anomaly samples to train detection model, which limits their application scope. Industrial discharge occurs less frequently, but the harm is very high. In order to detect industrial discharge, this paper presents an improved u-net model that only uses normal samples to train the model and has fewer network parameters, achieving effective detection of industrial discharge. The experiments show that the proposed method has high detection rate 98.26%, which can effectively detect industrial discharge.

articleTitle: Application Prospects of Large-Scale Model Technology in the Power Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Generative lager-scale model technology represented by GPT has become a historic turning point in the development of artificial intelligence, marking the transition of artificial intelligence technology from discriminative to generative. Under the new situation, the human-computer interaction mode has changed from single mode to multi-modal, the application form of artificial intelligence has changed from single to systematic, and the application mode has changed from perceptual intelligence to cognitive intelligence and decision-making intelligence collaboration. The next generation of artificial intelligence led by generative big model technology will have a profound impact on personal life, corporate production and even the entire social operation. Facing the vertical professional field of power grids, using big model technology to achieve a major change in the relationship between human and machine interaction, transform traditional business models, and promote architecture optimization and reshaping can be applied on a large scale in the power industry, becoming a new wave of digital transformation of power grids.

articleTitle: Effect of Virtual Images in Training Datasets on Highway Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Application of target detection in highway has been widely used nowadays to ensure safety and efficiency of traffic. However, the accuracy of target detection algorithms depends on a large size of datasets of real pictures of both vehicles and pedestrians. Obtaining these real pictures prove to be tedious work and time-consuming, which obviously impede fast implementation of target detection devices. Besides, real images incorporate lots of noises. In this paper, we attempt to use a mixture of virtual and real images for training in the target detection algorithms. The YOLOv5_6.0 algorithm is utilized. It is found that there exists an optimal proportion of virtual images in the training datasets to provide best recognition accuracy. Comparison of real and virtual images in training are discussed to provide insight and guidance on target detection using an optimal proportion of a mixture of real and virtual images.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Algorithm for Distribution Networks Based on Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: As power grids continue to expand, their structures become more complex, leading to an increased frequency of multiple faults, which presents a critical challenge for fault diagnosis. To tackle the issues of handling large volumes of fault data and the need for rapid and accurate fault diagnosis in power grids, this paper introduces a fault diagnosis model for distribution networks based on a fuzzy-optimized graph convolutional neural network (GCN). The methodology involves several steps: Data Processing: Collected characteristic data from distribution network fault lines are preprocessed. Model Construction: A fault diagnosis model based on GCN is developed, and the membership function for distribution network faults is established using fuzzy theory. Model Application: The trained model is utilized to diagnose distribution network faults. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the fuzzy-optimized GCN achieves higher accuracy in multi-fault diagnosis compared to conventional neural networks and alternative methods. The proposed method yields more precise diagnosis results, and overall, its diagnostic performance is superior..

articleTitle: The Transitivity of Actual Causation
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The tradition of counterfactual dependence to defining causation has come a long way since Lewis' creation. However, the open problems created by the imposed transitivity still wait to be resolved. This paper aims to formalize the Hitchcock definition of actual causation (2001) by using the structural equations framework of Halpern and pearl (2005), and provide sufficient conditions for actual causation to be transitive.

articleTitle: Research on Defect Detection in Printing Barcode Area Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The accuracy and aesthetics of information in the printing barcode area are of great significance in practical life. Flat printing defect detection is quite common, and there is currently almost no involvement in non flat printing defect detection. This work focuses on defect detection design for non flat printed barcode areas of glass bottles. After dividing the barcode area into two parts, barcode and character, we will perform defect detection on these two parts separately. For the barcode part, using support vector machines in machine learning to construct features and classify barcode defects. For the character part, a character quality evaluation method based on gray projection is adopted to output the character quality score. By combining the classification results of barcode defects with subjective judgment of quality scores, defect detection of barcode areas on non flat surfaces of glass bottles has been achieved.

articleTitle: Brain State Classification Based on Magnetoencephalography via Hybrid Linear-Dot Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The decoding of specific task activity patterns embedded in magnetoencephalography (MEG) is crucial for understanding brain function. As a kind of useful neuroimaging technology, MEG decoding plays a key role in Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI). In our study, the public MEG data were downloaded from the Human Connectivity Group Project (HCP), and the cascade model based on Hybrid Linear-Dot Attention Mechanics was proposed to conduct the brain decoding. The performance of the proposed model was evaluated by conducting cross-topic multiclassification verification on the MEG dataset under different states of subjects. Learned from the experiment, the highest accuracy and the F1 score were 69% and 63% on dataset 1, 92% and 92% on dataset 2, respectively. The proposed model has been demonstrated to enhance the classification performance of the Cascade model, proving its efficiency and practicality in the classification of MEG data.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Modal Decision-Making Intelligence Technology for Complex Power Operation Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the complexity of power business processes, higher requirements are put forward for multi-mode decision making.
