In this paper, a solution based on multi mode intelligent technology is proposed to solve the decision making problem in complex power business processes. First, it analyzes the challenges and demands in the power operation process, including changing environmental conditions, diverse task types, and multiple decision-making factors. Then, the advantages of multimodal intelligence technology in solving complex problems and its application potential in the field of electric power are introduced. Then, a decision model based on multi-modal data fusion and deep learning is proposed, which can obtain information from multiple data sources and realize intelligent decision by deep learning algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness and performance advantages of the proposed method are verified by experiments, and the future application prospect in power operation process optimization is forecasted.

articleTitle: Analysis the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on College Student Employment Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the continuous development of artificial intelligence(AI), its influence is becoming more and more extensive. The development of AI and the employment of college students are both hot topics in today's society. In order to analyze the situation of college students using AI technology and the impact of AI on the employment of college students. We crawled 2398 job recruitment information from the website and conducted a questionnaire survey of college students. Identifying the relatively popular professional fields under the context of AI, and binary logistic regression was used to model the factors affecting students' use of artificial intelligence technology. The research results provide a good reference for students' career planning.

articleTitle: Flexoelectric Effect to Understand Charge Transfer in Triboelectric Nanogenerators
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In this paper, the classical Hertzian contact theory with the flexoelectric effect is used to explain the charge transfer mechanism of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG). Through the analysis of mechanical deformation in the process of contact friction, a connection between mechanical deformation and friction charge density has been established by leveraging the flexoelectric effect. It is demonstrated that the surface potential difference generated by the electric field due to non-uniform deformation can serve as an intrinsic driving force for charge transfer. Finally, we consider the contact-separation mode, an important triboelectric nanogenerator, and study the output performance under various conditions.

articleTitle: High-Performance Network Firewall Based on XDP
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the development of computer technology, Internet technology has also witnessed rapid growth. However, the rapid expansion of the internet has led to an increase in the methods and diversity of cyberattacks, making network security a significant challenge that cannot be ignored in the global development of the internet. In the context of escalating cybersecurity threats and increasing network data traffic, enhancing the performance and effectiveness of firewall technology is crucial for strengthening network security protection and ensuring stable network operation. Traditional network firewalls operate in kernel mode, providing packet processing and filtering functions at the end of the protocol stack. When a large number of packets are discarded, it can lead to the CPU being occupied for a long time, resulting in significant resource waste. If packet processing can be done early in the packet reception process, it can greatly improve the performance of the firewall. To address the above issues, this article designs and implements a high-performance firewall technology based on the fast path packet processing capabilities of eXpress Data Path(XDP). With XDP technology, data packets can be processed at the earliest stage when they arrive at the network interface, without having to transfer the packets to the later stages of the kernel network stack. This approach offers better performance compared to traditional network firewall packet filtering methods.

articleTitle: FELSDiff: Image Super-Resolution Based on Diffusion Model Fusing Feature Extraction with Latent Space
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In addressing issues like an excessive number of network parameters and the loss of fine texture details in image super-resolution reconstruction approaches based on diffusion models, this passage introduces a novel image super-resolution model (FELSDiff). This model relies on the fusion of diffusion models, feature extraction, and latent space. FELSDiff utilizes a Pre-trained CNN for initial super-resolution to extract the primary low-band features and part high-band features of the image. The preliminary super-resolved image is then concatenated as a condition to this model. We introduce a cross-attention mechanism guided by the high-band features of the preliminary super-resolved image to enhance the network's feature extraction capability and obtain more effective features. In the U-Net structure, we incorporate a latent space strategy, enabling the model's training and inference processes to be conducted in the latent space, thereby reducing the number of network parameters. Experimental results on multiple standard datasets indicate that this method outperforms other advanced methods overall.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Standard Machine Learning and Multi-Business Transfer Adaptation Technology in Typical Power Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In response to the current standard discrimination models' poor adaptability to power business scenarios and the need for improved business understanding capabilities, this thesis focuses on the text embedding scenario in the standard digitalization of the power industry. It takes the standard data resources of the power industry as the starting point for research, studying the adaptation technology of standard machine learning for typical scenarios in the power industry, supporting the standard discrimination model to understand the standard discrimination business in typical scenarios; it studies the multi-business transfer adaptation technology for typical scenarios in the power industry, supporting the transfer of the power standard discrimination model that is adapted to the scenario to different businesses within the same application scenario; it studies the application verification and optimization of the standard discrimination model in typical scenarios of the power industry, enhancing the transferability of artificial intelligence discrimination models. This thesis is aimed at constructing an enhanced pre-trained model for power standard knowledge, realizing the application verification of the standard discrimination model in a typical scenario of power grid main equipment technical supervision based on automated differential comparison.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing Resource Load Prediction Based on the Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm Optimizing GRU-RNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Consider the inherent shortcomings of particle swarm optimization algorithm(PSO), this paper improves the inertia weight of the particle swarm optimization algorithm. We call this improved algorithm as IPSO. Then, IPSO is used to optimize the number of neurons in each layer of the GRU-RNN model. An IPSO-GRU-RNN prediction model based on improved particle swarm optimization is established to predict the resource load of cloud computing center. The experiment results show that the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm effectively optimizes the model parameters and improves prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: The Fire and Gas Control System of a Floating Gas Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the increasing demand for electricity in economic development and the emphasis on clean energy under the background of “double carbon”, Natural Gas (NG), as a lowcarbon fossil fuel, occupies an important position in the transitional period of the third global energy transition. Floating Gas Power Plant (FGPP) is a new type of power generation unit fueled by NG with characteristics of short construction period, high flexibility, and far away from residential areas, which is a good alternative to the traditional land-based NG power plant. In this paper, a fire and gas control system (F&GCS) is designed to ensure the fire and gas safety of FGPP. And the description, scope, characteristics, constitute parts of this F&GCS are detail described, as well as input devices and voting logic architectures. A case study of a new-built FGPP is presented, hope to provide a thought for the design of F&GCS for the similar type of floating plant.

articleTitle: On the Impact of the Large Population on Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: As population-based searching techniques, Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are ideal for solving real-world or black-box optimization problems. Due to the stochastic nature, there is a common viewpoint that a large population benefits solving difficult or complex problems if given enough runtime. To figure out the necessity of large populations, many theoretical works on sizing population have been proposed since 1990s regardless of the computing efforts. However, an interesting phenomenon is observed that two opposite views exist meanwhile. Most theoret-ical work admitted the benefits of a large population on solving difficult problems with a sufficient computing budget. While a few works claimed that a large population is unhelpful and it is only a waste of computing efforts. Therefore, a comprehensively experimental study that practically examines the benefits of a large population is necessary but still lacking due to the backward computing facilities in the past. However, benefiting from the modern parallel computing platforms, the computing capability is no longer the bottleneck and processing a great number of fitness evaluations (FEs) in a reason time is now practical. In this work, we systemically investigate the performance of EAs with a large population in terms of solution quality and computing speed on a GPU-enabled parallel computing platform. In order to comprehensively evaluate the impacts of a large population, two state-of-the-art and three generic algorithms are tested with population sizes ranging from small (64) to large (4096) on eight difficult problems for three dimensions. Results illustrate that not only EAs with a large population can achieve solutions with better quality but also run faster on a GPU-enabled parallel computing platform.

articleTitle: Classification of Similar Human Actions Using Based on Attention Mechanism and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In order to solve the shortcomings of traditional behavior classification methods in accurately distinguishing similar human behaviors, this study proposes a similar human behavior recognition method that integrates Transformer and YOLOv8 technology. This approach emphasizes key information in video content and associated human behavior characteristics, aiming to analyze human behavior through visual methods. It captures the dynamic characteristics of similar human behaviors between video frames by combining OpenPose and YOLOv8 technologies. With the help of the attention mechanism, this method can extract the features of important information in different environments. The detected action data and extracted features are jointly fed into the hybrid Transformer model to effectively classify similar human behaviors. The results of simulation experiments on the NTU-RGB+D dataset indicate that, compared to existing human behavior analysis techniques, this method is more effective in targeting the correlation of human behavior and demonstrates improved accuracy and sensitivity. the performance in terms of specificity and accuracy also exceeded other methods in the comparative experiments.

articleTitle: Accountability for User Actions: A Study on Aspects of Privacy and Misinformation in Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The ‘Web Revolution’ enabled easy access of internet and social media to everyone irrespective of demographic and financial challenges. Free internet services (at least in some countries) enabled easy access of information providing a big impact on spreading of misinformation and disinformation. Recently, the users of Virtual Reality environments like metaverse have been increasing posing the similar threats in virtual reality environment. Also, lack of regulations and systematic censoring has been a biggest concern for metaverse users. This study investigates the concerns around privacy and misinformation in virtual reality environment, asserting the existing regulations in place in general and a notable VRChat application in particular. A Metaverse Accountability Framework (MAF) is proposed to tackle some of the issues identified in the study emphasising the necessity of regulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Video-Based Real-Time Non-Contact Heart Rate Measurement Algorithm: Based on Third-Order Adaptive FastICA
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This work proposes a novel real-time non-contact heart rate measurement algorithm, which is based on the principle of heart rate estimation using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) technology. Initially, the study utilizes a webcam to detect and track human face. Due to the difference between skin color and the background, the algorithm segments the detected face to diminish unrelated disturbances. Subsequently, the FastICA algorithm has been enhanced by incorporating a dual relaxation factor to improve the stability of convergence and by upgrading FastICA to a third-order approach to increase processing speed. The signal is then subjected to wavelet packet threshold denoising to further mitigate high-frequency noise, thereby smoothing the signal. Eventually, the heart rate estimation is ascertained by counting the number of peaks within a signal window. Moreover, the paper introduces a sliding window technique, which facilitates real-time heart rate monitoring through the movement of the sliding window. Experiments conducted on the UBFC-rPPG dataset confirm that the heart rate measurements obtained with this algorithm are consistent with the actual heart rate values in the dataset and that the algorithm meets the requirements for real-time measurement.

articleTitle: Mining Periodic Patterns in an Attributed Graph Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Due to the wide application of attributed graph sequence data in real life, it is increasingly urgent to mine the periodic patterns in attributed graph sequences. The existing algorithms can only mine the periodic patterns in transaction databases and graph sequences, which cannot meet the need of periodic pattern mining in attributed graph sequences. Therefore, we extend the task of periodic pattern mining in a graph sequence to an attributed graph sequence, and propose a method for mining periodic patterns in an attributed graph sequence. We firstly transform the attributed graph sequence into a non-attributed graph sequence based on the method of attribute-extended graph. Then a new algorithm is designed to mine periodic patterns in a non-attributed graph sequence. By mining the periodic patterns in the transformed non-attribute graph sequence, all the periodic patterns in the original attributed graph sequence are obtained. Experiments on real data sets validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for periodic pattern mining.

articleTitle: Pathway and Empirical Study of Fire Accident Intelligence Support Based on Case Reasoning and Event Logic Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study aims to address the common and destructive disaster of fires by proposing an innovative intelligence support pathway to enhance the efficiency and quality of emergency decision-making. Traditional intelligence support faces challenges in handling fire accidents, such as insufficient construction of expertise databases, overlooking the dynamic nature of events, and a lack of quantitative research. Therefore, this research combines case-based reasoning and matter-element graph methods to improve decision quality by analyzing historical fire cases and establishing logical connections between events. A database including 128 fire cases was constructed, employing a combination of case-based and rule-based reasoning to generate decision-making support schemes. The study also utilized matter-element graphs to gain a deeper understanding of complex disaster situations. Empirical research was conducted using the fire incident at Beijing Changfeng Hospital as a case study. The study successfully matched the most similar case, optimized rules, and analyzed key links in the disaster chain and their interactions through the constructed matter-element graph. The research demonstrates the practical feasibility and effectiveness of the intelligence support pathway that combines case-based reasoning and matter-element graphs in emergency management of fires, providing theoretical and practical guidance for emergency decision-making in other fields. Moreover, this study's proposed approach, integrating qualitative and quantitative intelligence support, offers conceptual innovation and provides new theoretical perspectives for the construction of knowledge bases in specific fields.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Feature Selection with Fuzzy Clustering and Local Structure Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Feature selection is a crucial technique for handling high-dimensional data. In clustering analysis tasks, most feature selection methods typically involve selecting features using a projection matrix first, and then performing clustering with the selected features. However, these approaches may result in the selection of features during the initial stage that are not necessarily appropriate for subsequent clustering tasks. To deal with this matter, we proposes a strategy that combines fuzzy clustering with local structure learning for selecting features. We introduce fuzzy clustering to guide the process of feature selection, rather than solely relying on structural learning for feature selection. This approach effectively integrates two-stage models into a framework, enabling the acquisition of features that can represent both local structural information of the data and are suitable for clustering tasks, thereby enhancing the model's clustering performance. Moreover, we employ an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{2,0}$</tex> -norm constrained projection matrix for feature selection. This approach is easier to interpret than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{2,1}$</tex> -norm selection and eliminates the need for additional sorting operations, thus streamlining the feature selection process. It is worth emphasizing that we introduce a projection relaxation term. The presence of this projection relaxation term also makes the learned graph more flexible. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm has certain advantages over some classical algorithms.

articleTitle: Develop a New Method for Water Ecological Health Evaluation Incorporating Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the rapid development of China's society and economy, water ecological problems are becoming more and more prominent. This study proposes a new evaluation method of water ecological health. First, an evaluation index system based on the DPSIR model is constructed; second, a new water ecological health assessment model combining machine learning is constructed by integrating objective and subjective weights through game theory ideas, and the water ecological health status of Shaanxi Province in the past five years is comprehensively evaluated; finally, the temporal and space change characteristics of the watersheds in Shaanxi are deeply analyzed to reflect the water ecological health status of Shaanxi Province, and the interrelationship and influence between human activities and natural system, analyzing the interrelationships and impacts between human activities and natural systems, and revealing the urgency and criticality of water ecology management in Shaanxi Province. The study concludes with recommendations to ensure the long-term sustainable development of Shaanxi's water ecology, which will provide a scientific basis for future water resource management.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8 Network for Detecting UAV Aerial Image
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In this research, an improved version of the YOLOv8 network is proposed to mitigate the issue of low accuracy in the existing convolutional neural network-based aerial image detection model. The improvements include modifications to the neck structure, such as the addition of a tiny object detection layer and the removal of the large object detection layer. Additionally, a three-scale fusion module is integrated into the feature pyramid network (FPN) to facilitate a balanced transfer of semantic and positioning information across layers. An auxiliary head is introduced to offer supplementary gradient information for updating shallow network weights and balancing the distribution of positive and negative samples. Furthermore, enhancements are made to the C2f module of the neck structure to minimize redundant memory access. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8 network achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 47.6% on the VisDrone2019 dataset, representing a notable 7.1% improvement over the original network.

articleTitle: Environmental Performance Evaluation of Power Enterprises Based on a New Method
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the increasing attention of the state to environmental protection, enterprises are also gradually taking action to implement environmental protection work. As an industry with high carbon emission, the environmental performance evaluation of electric power enterprises is helpful for enterprises and the government to objectively understand the effect of environmental governance. However, the research on the environmental performance of the power industry is still lacking. Therefore, this paper takes Huadian Power International Corporation Limited, a representative power company, as the research object, and selects relevant data from 2019-2023 to establish an environmental performance evaluation index system. Firstly, the correlation degree between the selected indicators and environmental performance is verified based on grey correlation analysis. Secondly, the coefficient of variation method and entropy weight method are used for combined weighting. Finally, VIse Kriterijumski Optimizacioni Racun method is used for evaluation. The results prove that the indexes selected in this paper are reasonable, and each index has a strong correlation with environmental performance evaluation, and the environmental performance of Huadian is also improving year by year.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation via Inter- and Intra-Samples Relation Transferring
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model by learning the knowledge from a larger teacher. Recent approaches mostly emphasize spatial relation preserving between different samples, but ignore the geometrical manifold structure between semantic regions inside each sample. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach to learn relation information from inter- and intra-samples for robust student networks training. Different from traditional fully-connected relation constraints, our method contributes to preserving the local relation between each sample and its K-nearest samples to achieve a sparse inter-samples relation distillation, an easy and efficient way to train student networks. Meanwhile, the intra-sample distillation is designed to retain the spatial semantic information relation inside each sample. Both inter- and intrasamples relation are expressed as probability distributions, and KL divergence is used to measure the divergence between the probability distributions from teacher and student model, respectively. Experimental results, based on several different tasks: image classification, semantic segmentation and image-to-image translation, demonstrate that the proposed method exceeds the performance of other leading techniques.

articleTitle: HRRP Radar Target Recognition Based on Amplitude Spectrum Fractional Differentiation
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: The amplitude spectrum fractional differentiation (ASFD) feature extraction for high-resolution range profile (HRRP) and two-stage classification fusing strategy are proposed, motivated by the problem of radar automatic target recognition (RATR). Aircraft targets in HRRP data are mainly divided into turbine aircraft and propeller aircraft, and the surface structure and material characteristics of the two types of aircraft affect HRRP. When HRRP obtains amplitude spectrum characteristics through Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), ASFD will be extracted by fractional differentiation. This feature is helpful to solve the problem of low recognition rate of propeller aircraft. The two-stage classification fusion strategy is as follows: In the first stage, the propeller aircraft is selected based on the energy difference between adjacent amplitude spectra, and further selected from the high-order ASFD characteristics extracted from the remaining samples; In the second stage, low-order ASFD characteristics are extracted from the remaining amplitude spectrum characteristics selected in the first stage. This strategy can greatly improve the recognition rate of propeller aircraft. The ASFD characteristics of HRRP and the effectiveness of the two-stage classification fusion strategy are verified by the comparison experiments of minimum distance classifier, support vector machine (SVM) and one-dimensional convolution neural network (1DCNN).

articleTitle: Consistency analysis-based distance measure in Random Permutation Set Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Uncertain information frequently exists in the complex and diverse real-world environment. Probability theory and Dempster-Shafer theory respectively model uncertainty in the basic event space and the power set. To better characterize uncertain order information, Deng proposed the Random Permu-tation Set Theory, extending the power set to the permutation event space. This paper discussed the consistency in random permutation set divided into structural consistency and sequential consistency. Based on it, the consistency analysis-based distance measure has been proposed. This paper proposes a consistency analysis-based distance with its properties. Several numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Task Assignment Based on Improved Hybrid Frog Hopping Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low algorithm search efficiency, weak performance, slow convergence speed and easy to fall into local optimization in the multi-UAV task allocation problem, an improved hybrid frog leaping algorithm, also known as (Improve Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm, ISFLA) is proposed. On the basis of analyzing the task allocation model, the basic Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm (SFLA) is improved by introducing a reverse learning strategy and a firework explosion mechanism, which can effectively improve the diversity of the population; introducing a neighborhood learning strategy for the optimal individual, a dynamic jumping strategy for the worst individual, and introducing a Levy flight factor, which can effectively avoid the algorithm from falling into a local optimum early. The introduction of neighbor learning strategy for the optimal individuals, dynamic jumping strategy for the worst individuals and Levy flight factor can effectively avoid the algorithm from falling into the local optimum too early, and improve the search performance and convergence speed. The auction mechanism is utilized to cope with the dynamic task allocation in case of the unexpected situation when multiple UAVs perform the task cooperatively, which further improves the convergence performance of the algorithm. Simulation verification is carried out in different environment scales. Comparison results show that the improved hybrid frog jump algorithm improves the convergence speed and search accuracy in the multi-UAV task allocation problem.

articleTitle: Image Inpainting Based on High-Order Spatial Interaction Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Image inpainting is a fundamental task in the field of computer vision, aimed at using partially visible pixels in an image to repair missing or damaged parts of the image. In this paper, we propose a multi-stage cascaded image inpainting model based on high-order spatial interaction modules, which can achieve input adaption and long-range spatial interaction by introducing recursive gated convolutions in each high-order spatial interaction module, resulting in a global perceptual field and effective modeling of correlation between the inpainted region and the visible image range. Extensive experiments on CelebA-HQ dataset and Paris StreetView dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8s Algorithm for Distant Vessel Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Aiming at the phenomenon of missed detection and low detection rate of distant vessels in marine scenes, an improved model is proposed based on YOLOv8s (You Only Look Once). Firstly, in order to address the inefficiency of the original CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) in capturing global contextual information, the Swin-Transformer is used to replace the original CSP (Cross Stage Partial)-DarkNet in the backbone network section by utilizing self-attention mechanisms to learn long-term dependencies between different locations in image. Furthermore, in the Neck portion of the C2f module, a parallelized structure called CFLayer (Cross Fourier Layer) is added, which enhances the information obtained during multi-scale fusion by adding features from the frequency domain, thereby improving the detection accuracy of distant vessels. Finally, experimental tests were conducted on the distant vessel dataset Flow-Test. The results indicate that compared to the original YOLOv8s, the improved YOLOv8s has an increase in precision and recall rates of 0.9% and 0.8% respectively, and an increase in mAP (mean Average Precision) of 2.5%, effectively improving the detection accuracy of distant vessels.

articleTitle: A Python-Based Method for Translation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper explores a python-based data-driven method for translation quality assessment. The method depends on ratio of medium and long words, which is produced based on the Google's Trillion Word Corpus. The hypothesis of the research is that texts with high ratio of medium and long words are considered as academic and appropriate for translation of Chinese classics. The seven translations of Zhuangzi's Inner Chapters given by seven famous sinologists (including A.C. Graham, H.A. Giles, Martin Palmer, Robert Eno, Brook A. Ziporyn, Feng Youlan and Burton Watson) are used as texts to test this method. It is found that Giles' and Eno's translations are the top two best translations for they have the highest ratios of medium and long words proposed in this method. And then two other methods are provided to test the result for cross validation, i.e. the ratio of moderate and high-difficulty words and Type-Token Rate (TTR). And the two methods also produced similar results with the method of medium and long words. It can be concluded that the method of medium and long words proposed in this paper can be used for the assessment of Chinese classics as Zhuangzi's Inner Chapters.

articleTitle: Entity Extraction for Dispatching Automation Job Based on Knowledge Base
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the development of the electric power industry, the field of dispatch automation system operation and maintenance has accumulated a huge amount of unstructured data, and the historical data is difficult to be transformed into a priori knowledge, so the process of digital transformation in the field of power dispatch automation system operation and maintenance is slow. The use of knowledge graph to integrate multiple structural forms of data in power dispatch automation system helps to realize intelligent control and support the automation and intelligent transformation of dispatching operations. Entity extraction aims to extract the relationship between entities from massive and heterogeneous data, which is a key step in the construction of knowledge graph. In this paper, we propose an auxiliary method of entity extraction for dispatching automation job. Firstly, for the multimodal dispatching automation system's operation and maintenance data, text information was extracted through encoding, and text data preprocessing was conducted by combining the specific professional operation and management guidelines of power dispatching automation with the distinct data characteristics inherent to the system operation and maintenance domain; subsequently, text data redundancy was reduced through similarity computation, and ultimately, entities were extracted employing the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) algorithm to establish an entity knowledge base. Experiments show that the entity extraction knowledge base constructed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of entity extraction tasks.

articleTitle: Causal Structure Learning of High-Dimensional Data Based on Local and Global Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Causal learning in high-dimensional data environments faces challenges such as extracting complex causal relationships, dimensional explosion, and high computational complexity. Traditional causal discovery methods are divided into local and global approaches. Local methods are computationally efficient and suitable for capturing complex local structures but are not applicable to high-dimensional data. Global methods can capture extensive causal relationships but are computationally intensive. To address these issues, we propose a causal structure learning algorithm that combines local and global methods. This algorithm first partitions high-dimensional data into low-dimensional subsets through feature selection, with each subset independently generating its causal structure using a local algorithm. These structures are then merged into a global structure using the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), taking into account both the accuracy of the local structures and the rationality of the global structure. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that the proposed algorithm surpasses other state-of-the-art causal discovery algorithms in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Interactive Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Driving Based on the Combination of Riemannian Motion Policy and Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Vehicle lane changes during autonomous driving are a challenging task. In lane-changing scenarios, the presence of multiple vehicles and their interactions, combined with the lack of communication between vehicles, makes it difficult to perceive each vehicle's driving intentions, thereby creating safety risks. In this paper, we propose an interactive trajectory planning method in lane-changing scenarios, which proposes the reference position method as a motion policy to be deployed to the surrounding moving vehicles to achieve interaction with the surrounding vehicles; we introduce Riemannian Motion Policy (RMP) to allocate Riemannian metrics for multiple policies, addressing the impacts arising from interactions with different vehicles, combining Riemannian motion policy with an Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) network, utilizing an MLP network to perceive the driving environment and adjust the Riemannian metrics of different motion policies in real time, and the driving trajectories are generated by iterative computation through the Rollout method. Compared with most planning methods, this method propagates the impacts of interactions from the current moment to the next moment, making the generated trajectories conform to the actual kinematic constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RMP-MLP method can plan safe and smooth driving trajectories with good real-time performance, effectively simulating human driving behavior.

articleTitle: Linear Fuzzy Information Granule and Soft Subspace Based Multivariate Time Series Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In recent years, multivariate time series clustering has been widely concerned by scholars. However, the current studies on multivariate time series clustering are faced with two problems. That is, it is often difficult to eliminate the influence of redundant features, and deal with the situation where different clusters exist in different feature subspaces. To solve these two problems, this paper proposes a clustering algorithm for multivariate time series based on soft subspace. Inspired by the satisfactory performance of fuzzy information granulation in the field of time series clustering, especially linear fuzzy information granulation which portrays trend information in an interpretable manner, this paper designs a clustering algorithm based on Gaussian linear fuzzy information granules. Firstly, fuzzy information granulation of multivariate time series is performed, resulting in a multivariate granular time series. Then a clustering algorithm based on soft subspace is designed to cluster the multivariate granular time series. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in clustering multivariate time series according to varying shapes or trends.

articleTitle: A Method Based on Genetic Programming to Automatically Construct Factors for Annual Report Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Factors have always played an important role in stock analysis, but they are only effective for specific problems in specific scenarios. Therefore, constructing factors timely and quickly for different scenarios is an urgent problem to be solved. Although some experts have constructed factors, they need to manually construct factors for each scenario, and the construction process consumes time and effort. The annual report is an important and common scenario. It is an important form of information disclosure and financial reporting. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for automatically constructing factors based on genetic programming that combines expert experience for this scenario. It incorporates the knowledge and insights of experts in the field of stock analysis into the process of automati-cally constructing factors, and continuously adjusts and improves the combination of factors through genetic programming to adapt to the needs of the scenario. The effectiveness of this method is verified through empirical analysis and its advantages in specific scenarios are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Winograd-Based Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that convolutional neural networks need to consume a large number of computational units and have a high computational complexity in embedded systems, this paper proposes a Dedicated Hardware Accelerator for VGG16-XDSC network based on Winograd algorithm. VGG16-XDSC is a lightweight network that consists of Depthwise Convolution and Shared Kernel sliding on channel Convolution, which is able to reduce the computational complexity and model size of the network while maintaining high accuracy. In order to further improve the computational efficiency of VGG16-XDSC, a series of accelerated optimization methods are proposed on the hardware side, including the shared computation engine of 1D Winograd and 2D Winograd, the merging processing unit of input transformations and the corresponding elemental multiplication, and avoiding the repetitive row transformation operations through row transformation optimization, utilizing the principle of 1D convolution kernel decomposition and the operations such as the 16-bit moving point quantization which further improves the computational efficiency of the network. The experimental results show that in the synergistic acceleration through algorithms and hardware architecture, the VGG16-XDSC gas pedal based on the Ultra96 V2 FPGA development board achieves 30.1 FPS with only 268 DSPs, and the energy efficiency reaches 13.44 GOPS/W, which accelerates the VGG16 more than ordinary Hardware accelerators.

articleTitle: Ensemble-based Offline Data-driven Evolutionary Optimization for Operation Parameter of Blast Furnace
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Stable control of the iron-making process through the adjustment of operating parameters is essential to improve blast furnace productivity. However, due to the complex and dynamic nature of the reaction process, it is difficult to perform accurate modeling and simulation experiments for a blast furnace. This poses great difficulties in performing the evaluation of control strategies in real-time. Offline evolutionary optimization, as an optimization technique that relies only on historical data, enables the search for optimal operation parameters through the introduction of surrogates. Based on the characteristics of historical time-series data of the iron-making process, this study proposes an offline evolutionary optimization method based on advanced time-series surrogates. Ensemble strategy combining surrogates with different prediction time windows contributes robustness during the optimization process. Additionally, multiple sub-regions are maintained to enable extensive searching of the decision space with a multi-objective nature. The efficiency of the proposed pooling method is demonstrated through verification in actual production cases.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hardware Equipment of Broadband Channel Simulator Based on Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the rapid development of global communication technology and the gradual improvement of 5G network, the communication industry is facing more and more challenges, including complex channel transmission problems such as delay, fading and Doppler effect. In order to simulate the real communication scene efficiently in the laboratory environment, a broadband channel simulator for Ka-band is proposed in this paper. The device can simulate the transmission characteristics of channel and realize the transmission and receiving of two-channel signals. It has the characteristics of high frequency, large bandwidth and modularity. The research work includes the theoretical analysis of the channel simulator, the design of the component architecture, and the realization of the hardware solution suitable for Ka-band. The design of the simulator is mainly composed of frequency conversion module and baseband module. The frequency conversion module is responsible for the conversion of Ka-band and IF signal, while the baseband module processes IF signal through analog-to-digital conversion and channel simulation algorithm, and finally outputs analog signal through digital-to-analog conversion. This kind of hardware equipment provides a feasible and economical means to study and solve the problems in the complex communication environment.

articleTitle: The New Digital Human Application Technology Based on the Man-Machine Collaborative Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the continuous progress of science and technology, UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) technology has been widely used in the field of the electric power inspection. However, the traditional UAV inspection system has some limitations in human-computer interaction and the intelligent processing capability in complex environments. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a new digital human application technology based on man-machine cooperative operation and applies it to electric power UAV inspection operation. By introducing digital people, the technology improves the human-machine interaction of the UAV inspection system, and realizes the intelligent processing and analysis of the inspection data. To verify the high efficiency and accuracy of the proposed system, experimental studies were performed here. The experimental results show that, compared with the traditional UAV inspection system, the UAV inspection system based on digital human technology has significant advantages in improving the inspection operation efficiency, reducing human error, and reducing labor cost and risk. In addition, this paper also discusses the development trend and the potential innovation direction of digital human technology in the field of electric UAV inspection, which provides a useful reference for future research in related fields. In conclusion, this paper provides an innovative solution for the field of electric UAV inspection by studying a new digital human application technology based on human-machine collaborative operation. The research results have important reference value for promoting the development and application of electric UAV inspection technology.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Analysis Method for Multi-Stage Web Attack Forensics
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In this paper, we propose IVMWAF, a framework for intelligent analysis of multi-stage web attacks which uses artificial intelligence and visualization approaches. The IVMWAF framework is designed to provide a general and practical forensic process for investigating multi-stage web attacks. Using IVMWAF, digital forensics analysts can have a flexible and intuitive understanding of the overall situation of complex web security incidents. Specifically, in order to extract all web security incident related anomalies, we first propose a multi-level anomaly detection method, by dividing different levels based on different stages of the web attack chain. We also design methods for visualizing and making human-computer interactions for different levels of anomaly detection, to assist analysts in comprehending and providing feedback on the decisions made by intelligent methods. For forensic analysis of web attack incidents, we integrate multi-level anomaly detection and visualization for correlation analysis, and propose a method for constructing multi-level web attack scenarios. Finally, we developed a prototype system and validated the usability and superiority of the proposed IVMWAF with experimental results and expert evaluations on a dataset during a real enterprise security incident.

articleTitle: Genetic Programming for Feature Learning and Feature Construction in Glioma Survival Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: MRI imaging plays a vital role in the initial tumor screening process and also aids in constructing a high-dimensional feature space for survival prediction tasks through the combination of sequences and tumor subregions. Traditional GP methods applied to feature construction treat features as part of the terminal set, which limits their search capabilities. Combining feature learning with GP allows for the direct use of image data, albeit dependent on predefined extraction functions. Our goal is to design a FLFC method that integrates feature learning and construction to automatically locate ROIs, extract features, construct new features, and match classifiers in 3D MRI images. To this end, we have introduced a new GP structure with an interpretable function set. To verify the algorithm, experiments were performed using the publicly available BraTS 2020 dataset. Ours achieved an average accuracy of 94.14% in the binary classification task (differentiating between HGG and LGG) and 72.49% in the four-class task (within HGG subtypes). These results underscore the efficacy of the FLFC method in harnessing the complexity of MRI data for meaningful survival prediction, illustrating its potential as a robust tool in medical imaging analysis and cancer prognosis.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Multi-Scale Fine-Tuning Samples for Electric Power Based on the Chain of Thought
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Currently, the power sector is characterized by the dispersion of data across different times, spaces, or complexities, as well as difficulties in the unified collection of sample data, leading to significant challenges in obtaining multi-scale fine-tuning samples. In light of this, this paper focuses on the collection and preprocessing of textual data in the power sector and proposes a method for constructing multi-scale fine-tuning samples in the power sector based on the chain of thought. By introducing multi-scale analysis methods, power system data is divided according to different temporal and spatial scales, thereby creating a sample set with hierarchical structure and diversity. This method can adaptively adjust the selection and enhancement strategies of samples based on the characteristics of data at different scales, thus effectively representing and modeling the complex data of the power system and improving the efficiency and accuracy of text data processing in the power sector.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotion Perception in Sentiment Analysis through Large-Scale Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Traditional sentiment analysis methods often overlook the sensitivity to emotional changes in text, which limits their applicability in real-world scenarios. To address this issue, We presents a deep learning based Sentiment-Aware Analysis Model(SAAM), leveraging the powerful representation capability of large-scale language models, namely the sentiment-aware world model introduced herein, in conjunction with the sentiment-sensitive SAAM. Through experimental validation, we demonstrate the effectiveness and performance advantages of the proposed algorithm in sentiment analysis tasks, highlighting the significant role of large-scale language models in sentiment-aware analysis. This approach provides new insights and methods for the field of sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: CFR: CNN Visual Framework Based on ResNet for Person Re-Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Person re-identification (Re-ID) has advanced rapidly, propelling technology to new heights. However, the models are also growing increasingly intricate. Different models and more potent feature extraction models have been developed as a result of current research. They are all hampered, meanwhile, by having a large number of parameters and a complex model. The CNN Visual Framework based on ResNet (CFR) module, which consists of three parts-a CNN-based Feature Extraction (CFE), a Multi-scale Feature Extractor (MFE), and a Hierarchical Feature Aggregation (HFA)-is introduced in this succinct Re-ID model. These modules incorporate several loss functions and enhance the model's capacity to extract important information. The results of the experiments indicate that tests were performed on three prominent Re-ID datasets, achieving strong performance on two of them: on the dataset Market1501, Rank-1 is 94.40%, and mAP is 87.30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and on the dataset, DukeMTMC, Rank-1 is 88.30%, and mAP is 78.90%.

articleTitle: Deciphering Children's Social Cognition: Leveraging NLP for Deeper Insights Into Social Role Perceptions
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This research uses natural language processing (NLP) methods to explore how children of varying genders and ages perceive social roles. By analyzing interview responses from 184 first- and fifth-grade French children, the study investigates their thoughts and beliefs about the concept of “friend.” Through a specialized NLP technique, the study categorizes the most common lemmas, revealing three main themes: similarity, support/intimacy, and association/affection. Statistical analyses of these patterns provide a deeper understanding of how children comprehend and interpret this social role. This research offers a unique perspective by focusing on the children's viewpoint, which contrasts with studies that mainly reflect the adult perspective.

articleTitle: Unbiased Estimators for Uniform Distribution Applied to Interval Estimation of Transition or Beginning Year About World Reserve Currency
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper firstly explores the maximum likelihood unbiased estimator, which is a prevalent method for parameter estimation in statistics, also an important tool of knowledge discovery. We begin by clarifying the fundamental concepts and properties of the maximum likelihood unbiased estimator. Through meticulous mathematical derivation, potential issues, such as bias that may arise when handling finite samples, are underscored. To mitigate these challenges, the maximum likelihood unbiased estimator is introduced, illustrating its capability to uphold high accuracy and stability, even within the context of finite and small samples. This paper delves into the nature and application of this improved maximum likelihood unbiased estimator, and then (i.e., secondly) explores the historical transitions of world reserve currency (WRC), which is a global monetary standard facilitating international trade and finance. WRC transitions (WRCT), typically lasting 80–110 years, signal significant transformations in global economic order and power dynamics. Over the past 500 years, five such transitions have occurred, each marking the rise and fall of nations. The transitions were driven by changes in market demand and financial markets, leading to shifts in economic paradigms. Also based on the additional exploration of WRC beginning (WRCB) years, the paper finally (i.e., thirdly) suggests that we may be on the brink of another major transformation, as the USA dollar, the current WRC, should follow the historical cycle. By studying these patterns, we gain insights into future global economic trends, which is a hot topic of recently interesting WRC financial knowledge discovery. Simply summarize: the coming (or termed this round) WRCT year is within [2008, 2047], and the coming WRCB year is within [2008, 2057].

articleTitle: Bipartite Recommendation Algorithm of Knowledge Graph and Graph Convolution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Addressing the issue that most current Knowledge Graph-based recommendation algorithms primarily focus on feature extraction from either the user or the item side, leading to suboptimal recommendation performance, a bipartite recommendation algorithm of knowledge graph and graph convolution network (BKGCN) is proposed. First, a neighborhood aggregation approach captures the higher-order relationships between each layer of the entity network, providing an initial description of the entities and browsing records in the user, project, and knowledge graphs. Next, by utilizing both the user and item sides to extract features, a knowledge-aware attention network based on users and items computes the internal information of triples. Finally, the neighborhood information obtained through the attention network from both the user and item sides is aggregated. The interaction probability between users and items is calculated using the inner product and normalization operations of the vectors. Utilizing two widely accessible datasets, namely Music Last.FM and Book-Crossing, comprehensive evaluations are undertaken through click-through rate prediction and Top-K recommendation tests, substantiating the effectiveness of the BKGCN algorithm. In comparison to the six foundational algorithms, BKGCN exhibits an enhancement of 1.4% in AUC and 0.3% in F1 over the best-performing baseline model on the Last.FM dataset. As for the Book-Crossing dataset, there is a notable improvement of 3.7% in AUC and 2.2% in F1, respectively. The experimental outcomes indicate that the algorithm demonstrates excellent performance in terms of recommendation effectiveness.

articleTitle: Effectiveness Evaluation and Improvement Path of Express Delivery to Village Based on Capability Maturity
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Express delivery to the village is to realize the effective connection between farmers and the market, stimulate the potential of rural consumption, is the key to achieve rural revitalization. Based on the standards of capability maturity Model and relevant theoretical research, this paper defines the maturity of express delivery into villages as five levels: Initiation level, accessibility level, access level, optimization level and Sustainability level. The maturity model of express delivery to villages is constructed, which includes six indexes: annual delivery volume, annual collection volume, number of township outlets, number of village outlets, and number of transport vehicles and mileage of post roads. Then, the entropy weight-TOPSIS method was used to calculate each parameter in the model. Taking some counties in Shaanxi, Gansu and Shandong as the research object, the maturity of express delivery to villages was evaluated based on the data of each county's postal administration bureau, county government and express delivery enterprises in 2023, and specific values were calculated to describe the maturity of the project and verify the practicality of the model. This model can provide a method and tool for evaluating the maturity of express delivery to villages in China, and can also provide a reference for establishing the target system of express delivery to villages, constructing the evaluation model of implementation effect, and reasonably evaluating the current implementation situation.

articleTitle: An Interview System Based on Large Language Models and Multi-Agent Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: To address the increasing demand for interviews, we have proposed an intelligent interview system. This system has the capability to generate interview questions and design interview processes. This system introduces a ChatGPT-based iterative enhancement algorithm for seed datasets to create a high-quality prompt-question dataset specific to the interview domain. Through large-scale language model fine-tuning, the system can generate more accurate and expected interview questions, demonstrating significant performance improvements across multiple evaluation metrics. Additionally, the study introduces an innovative multi-agent interaction algorithm to enhance interview process efficiency and comprehensive information gathering. Experimental results indicate improvements in text coherence and contextual understanding with the fine-tuned model, and subjective testing confirms the system's fluency and practicality.

articleTitle: A Spectrum Prediction Network Based on Time-Frequency Correlation Fusion Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the development of modern communication technology, the electromagnetic spectrum environment is becoming increasingly complex. Frequency Spectrum Prediction is an important technology in Cognitive radio (CR). It plays a significant role in spectrum user authorization management, spectrum resource scheduling and spectrum interference avoidance. Traditional spectrum prediction methods are susceptible to noise and its performance is limited when the amount of spectral data is large. Therefore, we designed a Time-Frequency Correlation Capture module as a network branch for correlation feature extraction. We also designed the multi-scale Decoder module to build a spectrum prediction model based on Sequence-to-Sequence architecture deep network. The dataset is generated by using software radio equipment to collect electromagnetic environment around the campus. As verified by the measured spectrum data, our method improves significantly in spectrum multi-channel prediction compared with the traditional method and existing networks.

articleTitle: DDoS Detection and Defense Based on FLAD and SDN
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In order to achieve more efficient and accurate DDoS detection while ensuring data privacy, this paper proposes a DDoS detection method based on FLAD. Firstly, this paper uses the FLAD algorithm to train a global DDoS detection model without leaving local traffic data, protecting the privacy and security of traffic data between different hosts, and improving aggregation efficiency by dynamically adjusting the aggregation weights to adapt to different sub-dataset increments. Secondly, a DDoS traffic detection method based on the integration of LSTM and CNN is proposed, which extracts and analyzes the temporal correlation of traffic data by calculating the statistical characteristics of traffic data within a time period, to achieve real-time detection of traffic feature data. Again, combined with the concept of SDN, real-time defense against DDoS based on ODL-API is implemented, and precise matching of DDoS detection results with network entity information is achieved, realizing the technology of real-time and precise issuance of multiple flow rules, effectively blocking DDoS malicious attack traffic, protecting important entities in the topology, and maintaining stable traffic in the topology. This paper focuses on solving the detection problem of DDoS traffic data increments and uneven data distribution through the FLAD algorithm. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves the accuracy of DDoS attack detection by more than 4% and the F1 Score by more than 7% compared to the FedAvg aggregation algorithm.

articleTitle: How do Governments and Consumers Influence Multinational Corporations’ Emission Reduction Strategies? A Multi-Scenario-Based Evolutionary Game Study
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Multinational corporations (MNCs) play an important role in achieving carbon neutrality. To study the emission reduction strategies and paths of MNCs, this paper constructs a four-party evolutionary game model, including MNC subsidiaries, parent companies, local governments, and consumers. The model considers consumers’ preferences, the dual constraints of the regional policies of subsidiaries and parent companies on MNCs. The main conclusions are: (1) Increasing the carbon trading price can make subsidiaries and consumers the first to approach the ideal steady state, but is adverse to active government regulation; (2) The increase in the subsidy coefficient will positively promote the subsidiary to make positive emission reduction, but when the subsidy coefficient increases to a certain threshold, the government will be less willing to choose a regulatory strategy; (3) Appropriately reducing the price difference between low-carbon and non-low-carbon products is an effective way to promote consumers’ adoption of low-carbon consumption. This paper summarizes the optimal emission reduction strategies for MNCs from the perspective of a quadripartite evolutionary game, which provides theoretical support and a decision basis for MNCs to adopt emission reduction measures.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Learning Interest Topic Tracking Method
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence, the Internet and other technologies with education, smart online education has become a hot topic in the current education field. Compared with traditional education methods, online education has the advantages of flexibility in time and space, convenience in sharing learning resources, and autonomy in learning for students. The online learning platform has rich interactive activities and generates a large amount of multi-channel learning behavior data. However, the large number of learners objectively leads to the problem of low teacher-student ratio, and teachers often cannot pay attention to each learner. Mining learners' characteristics, and then realizing personalized guidance is one of the core problems to be solved urgently in the large-scale education environment. The experiment illustrates the effectiveness of our proposed method and has practical application value.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Segmentation Method of Dermatological Images Based on DeepLabV3+ with Dual Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This study introduces the development of an enhanced DeepLabV3+ algorithm for skin lesion image segmentation, which integrating a Dual Attention Mechanism Module (DAMM) to improve feature extraction capabilities. The study employed two connection strategies for incorporating DAMM with the Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP): serial and parallel configurations. Initially, several models such as U-Net, Attention U-Net (ATU-Net), Fully Convolutional Networks-ResNet101 (FCN-ResNet101), DeepLabV3, DeepLabV3+ and FCN32s were comparatively analyzed, and finally the DeepLabV3+ was identified as the most potential models, which achieving a Jaccard index of 0.7989. Subsequently, comparative assessment of the two modified DeepLabV3+ models featuring the dual attention mechanism highlighted their superior performance in the segmentation task, with the parallel model notably increasing the Jaccard index to 0.8144, an improvement of 1.55% over the original. Additionally, when compared against the segmentation models of competitors from the ISIC 2018 Challenge, the parallel DAMM-ASPP configuration demonstrated a 1.24% increase in the Jaccard index over the best-performing team, validating the efficacy of this innovative composite structure for accurate segmentation of skin lesions.

articleTitle: Non-destructive Ripeness Judgement of Watermelon Based on Mel Spectrogram and ECAPA-DTNN
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In daily life, the majority of consumers generally have little professional knowledge to select ripe watermelons. However, the laboratory non-destructive methods for judging the ripeness of watermelon has limitations and is not suitable for consumers. Obviously, it is important and practical to develop a method for judging the ripeness of watermelon that is convenient for consumers. In this study, we utilized portable smartphones to record watermelon tapping audio signals of different ripeness levels and established a dataset. Then, we preprocessed the recorded audio signals. Next, we extracted Mel spectrogram features from the audio signals in the frequency domain using Short Time Fourier Transform and Mel Filter Bank. Finally, we used these features as input to train the ECAPA- TDNN model. The experimental results show that the accuracy of 89.5% on the test set, demonstrating that this method can achieve non-destructive judging of watermelon ripeness in daily life and is suitable for the majority of consumers.

articleTitle: Research on Enhanced Perception and Attention-Driven Person Re-Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: When matching similarity among pedestrians in images, pedestrian re-identification algorithms are often disturbed by occlusions. A typical tactic is to improve the robustness of occlusion features in the model. However, this approach neglects the noise introduced by other pedestrians in the image, leading to limited learning of relevant information between images. To address these issues, this paper introduces a pedestrian re-identification model that leverages perception-enhanced and attention mechanisms. By enhancing the perception of non-pedestrian noise and erasing non-pedestrian features, we then employ a cross-attention mechanism to subtly embed global and local features for finer feature recognition. Finally, through context attention, we learn the interaction between pedestrian images to improve re-identification accuracy. Results from studies performed on the Market-1501, CUHK03-D, and Duke-ReID datasets indicate that the suggested model surpasses leading contemporary models regarding Rank-1 scores and mean Average Precision (mAP), while maintaining good robustness.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Spectrum Sensing of Sub-Nyquist Sampled Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Traditional Nyquist rate sampling faces significant challenges as communication technology progresses towards 6G. Multi-coset sampling emerges as a viable solution by reducing the sampling rate. However, this method necessitates signal restoration before processing. In response, an intelligent spectrum management system has been developed that utilizes deep learning to directly extract semantic information from multi-coset sampled signals, eliminating the need for complex data preprocessing. The system integrates multi-band spectrum sensing and modulation recognition, achieving an impressive 99% accuracy in both modulation recognition of single signals and sub-band positioning of multiple signals.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Knowledge Unified Representation Learning Method Adapted to Dynamic Data Update for Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: In typical power industry applications, the multimodal knowledge graph faces the challenges of difficulty in integrating and utilizing modal information, and difficulty in dynamically adjusting knowledge representation as the graph is updated. To address this issue, this paper proposes a unified representation learning method for multi-modal knowledge graphs suitable for typical power business applications. Firstly, a unified representation learning framework is proposed for multi-modal knowledge graphs tailored for typical power businesses. Secondly, a knowledge representation learning technique that integrates entity descriptions and hierarchical information is introduced. Thirdly, a knowledge representation learning technique based on attention mechanism is proposed to integrate solid image information. Finally, a unified representation updating method is presented for multimodal knowledge graphs with dynamic data updates. The experimental results illustrate that the proposed method can efficiently fusion and update the power multi-modal knowledge, and provide unified support for knowledge-driven tasks such as information retrieval, interaction and reasoning based on knowledge graph.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Power Business Analysis Application Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, the power industry is also constantly exploring how to use AI-driven technology to improve business processes and increase efficiency. This paper will focus on AI-driven power business analysis application technology, including its application in power production, power transmission and distribution, energy management and market analysis. We will introduce various application cases of AI technology in the power field and explore its potential advantages in improving energy utilization, optimizing power supply systems, and predicting energy demand and prices. Finally, we will also discuss the challenges and future development trends that AI technology may face in the power industry.

articleTitle: Development of a High-Precision Multi-Source Localization System Based on DUET-SRP-PHAT
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: Sound Source Localization (SSL) is an important front-end technology in the field of speech and audio signal processing, widely used in machine fault diagnosis, sound recognition, intelligent conferences, and other fields. This article proposes a high-precision SSL method based on DUET-SRP-PHAT and develops a high-precision multi-source localization system. After collecting data through a microphone array, the system uses Degradation Unmixing Estimation Technology (DUET) to separate the mixed signal into source signals and then uses the Steered Response Power with Phase Transform (SRP-PHAT) algorithm to estimate time delay and analyze the position of the sound source. At the same time, the three-dimensional image of the sound source through the upper computer software makes the localization of the sound source more intuitive. Through experiments, it has been shown that the proposed method has an error of less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6^\mathrm{o}$</tex> in single-source and dual-source localization, and less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8^{\circ}$</tex> in three-source localization. This indicates that the developed system has high accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Intuitionistic Fuzzy Portfolio Decision Model Based on Possibilistic Skewness
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
abstract: This paper employs intuitionistic fuzzy numbers to flexibly evaluate the expected returns of assets, and uses intuitionistic fuzzy possibilistic mean, variance to characterize return and risk of portfolio. An intuitionistic fuzzy portfolio decision model with investment dispersity and scale is constructed by maximizing portfolio skewness while satisfying the portfolio return is greater than the given desired level and the variance risk is less than the given tolerance. Then, a differential evolution algorithm is utilized to quickly solve the proposed portfolio decision model with multiple nonlinear constraints. Finally, a numerical example of real stock data is used to illustrate the effectiveness of the presented model.

articleTitle: Discrimination Method of Processed Traditional Chinese Medicine Products Based on Near-Infrared Spectroscopy and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
